title: A sub-plan calling another sub-plan
idea: Composing functions: a sub-plan's BODY can call another sub-plan and use its returned value. Composition lives inside a definition too.

exercises.explanation: double_plus_one calls double(5) -> 10, then adds 1 -> 11. A sub-plan can use another sub-plan inside its body.

exercises.prompt: A sub-plan's body is allowed to call another sub-plan and use its returned value.
exercises.explanation: Yes. Inside double_plus_one, the call double(n) runs and its returned value is used in the + 1. Composition inside a def.

options: double(n) — it returns a value, then + 1 is added
exercises.explanation: The inner call double(n) resolves to a value first; then + 1 is added; then that result is returned.

exercises.prompt: Why is building double_plus_one on top of double a good idea?
options: It reuses double instead of repeating its logic
exercises.explanation: Reusing double avoids rewriting 'n * 2'. If double ever changes, double_plus_one benefits automatically.
Call double(n) to get n * 2, then add 1. The body composes with the other sub-plan.
double(10) is 20; + 1 is 21. The sub-plan reuses double for any input.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: define double, define area_doubled that returns double(width * height), then print area_doubled(3, 4).
exercises.explanation: area_doubled computes width * height = 12, feeds it to double -> 24. Composition inside a def, then a call.
width * height is 12; double(12) is 24. The inner math runs, then double doubles it.

exercises.prompt: For a sub-plan to use another's result inside its body, that other sub-plan must RETURN a value.
exercises.explanation: Yes. You can only use a value that's handed back. A printing-only sub-plan would give None inside the body.

options: A sub-plan can call another sub-plan in its body and use the returned value
exercises.explanation: Composition isn't only for the main plan — a sub-plan's body can reuse another sub-plan's returned answer.
